elements.heroSubtitle: Reception, social support and defence of the rights of refugees, people seeking international protection and exiled people in Brussels.

maintext.p1: Founded in 1937 to support refugees from the Spanish Civil War, SESO is active in the fields of social work and migration. We provide individual and personalised support to the people who use our services, especially migrants and refugees, while respecting their autonomy, fundamental rights, right to family life and privacy. We promote tolerance, respect for rights, the fight against all forms of discrimination, free inquiry, social justice and emancipation.

ssg.title: General Social Service
paragraphs: Our General Social Service provides first-line general social assistance for anyone, with or without a residence permit.

Over many years, our General Social Service has developed expertise in foreigners' law. We support people in areas such as residence, social security, the right to work, training and studies, housing, debt and health.
Our support aims to strengthen social connection and improve access to collective facilities and fundamental rights.

dpi.title: Reception and support for asylum seekers
paragraphs: SESO has set up a reception structure for asylum seekers under an agreement with Fedasil.
This reception is based on the law of 12 January 2007 on the reception of asylum seekers and certain other categories of foreign nationals.
In practical terms, this reception is organised through individual housing and is subject to quality standards agreed with our partners. We have housing in Brussels, Flanders and Charleroi.

mena.title: Unaccompanied Foreign Minors (MENA)
paragraphs: This service deals with the situation of unaccompanied foreign minors. Aware of the social urgency facing this public, our association launched this service in June 2007 with social workers acting as guardians.
Our objective is to find a durable solution together with the young person. We support them throughout their journey until they reach adulthood or until the end of their procedure.

reab.title: Voluntary return (REAB)
paragraphs: Voluntary return assistance consists of a return ticket, which may be accompanied by a grant and reintegration support. Access to these forms of support depends on the applicant's administrative profile.
The person opens their file with our REAB service, where they have an initial interview to learn about the different options that may be available to them.
These funds may be used for regular education, specific training, the creation of micro-enterprises, housing costs, goods, document translation or job-search support.

ssg.title: General Social Service
paragraphs: The Social Service for Solidarity (SESO) aims to provide individual and personalised help to every person, especially people in migration, while respecting their autonomy, fundamental rights, right to family life and privacy. We promote tolerance, respect for rights, the fight against all forms of discrimination, free inquiry, social justice and emancipation.

Our General Social Service provides first-line general social assistance to people facing difficulties. We offer an initial welcome during individual interviews or drop-in hours in French, Dutch, English or Spanish. When needed, we also work with interpreters. We analyse the person's situation and set up social and administrative follow-up.

Over many years, our General Social Service has developed expertise in foreigners' law. We support people with asylum, family reunification, single permit applications, residence regularisation and access to nationality.

dpi.title: Reception structure for people seeking international protection
paragraphs: Created through agreements with Ciré asbl and FEDASIL, SESO asbl’s DPI reception structure aims to receive and support people seeking international protection who are in vulnerable situations and have specific medical, social, psychological and/or educational needs.

The service supports an average of 150 to 180 people per month, with varied profiles and levels of vulnerability. Support is individualised, coordinated and adapted to each person’s needs, with the goals of stabilising the situation, enabling access to rights and care, improving living conditions and gradually developing autonomy.

The people supported include adults with significant medical needs, including people with serious or chronic conditions requiring regular medical follow-up and care coordination; “High-Care” situations involving serious medical issues and/or complex vulnerabilities requiring reinforced support; unaccompanied foreign minors (MENA), requiring social, educational, administrative and medical support adapted to their age and journey; and people needing an individual housing environment, including LGBTQI+ people facing discrimination, family breakdown or precariousness, as well as single-parent families with young children.

The DPI reception structure is based on a global and multidisciplinary approach combining social support, educational follow-up, psychosocial support, access to care and referral to specialised services. Particular attention is paid to coordination between the different actors and partners to ensure continuity and coherence in each pathway.
Within SESO, this service therefore provides support adapted to multiple and complex vulnerabilities, with concrete, individualised and evolving responses to the needs of the people received.

mena.title: Unaccompanied Minors
paragraphs: The MENA guardianship service was created in 2007 with the recruitment of two guardians. The team currently consists of eight guardians, an administrative assistant/school referent and a coordinator.
The guardians are accredited by the Guardianship Service of the FPS Justice. Each guardian is individually linked to the young people entrusted to them.
The Guardianship Service increased the subsidies allocated to associations employing guardians. The aim is to professionalise this role as much as possible.

Since 1 June 2026, four guardians have been hired as part of the entry into force of the European migration pact. Their mission is to support young people from their arrival at the registration centre until their transfer to a second-phase centre.
There are French-speaking and Dutch-speaking guardians. The Guardianship Service aims to professionalise guardianship through associations.
The guardian is the legal representative of the unaccompanied foreign minor. In this capacity, they ensure respect for the young person’s rights and overall well-being.
Carrying out these missions requires close collaboration with lawyers specialised in foreigners’ law, various social services, schools, reception centres, health services and many other partners.

The guardian is accredited and supervised by the Guardianship Service. This supervision is reinforced by the Justice of the Peace, who intervenes in case of disputes between guardians and their wards.
services: ensure access to suitable accommodation, in a reception centre or with a family
support all administrative and legal procedures
support the young person in finding the durable solution most consistent with their best interests
support residence applications based on Article 61/15 of the law of 15 December 1980, known as the durable solution procedure
support temporary protection applications for specific groups, including young Ukrainians

reab.title: Return and reintegration of asylum seekers from Belgium
paragraphs: Since 1984, the Belgian State has entrusted the REAB programme to the IOM. Our Social Service works in partnership with the IOM and helps people open a return file.

Voluntary return assistance consists of a return ticket, which may be accompanied by a grant and reintegration support. Access to these forms of support depends on the applicant's administrative profile.
These funds may be used for regular education, specific training, the creation of micro-enterprises, housing costs, goods, document translation or job-search support.
This humanitarian programme assists migrants in need who wish to return voluntarily and reintegrate in their country of origin. It is intended for three categories of migrants in Belgium:

categories.label: Asylum seekers:
categories.text: migrants who have applied for asylum and are waiting for a final decision.

categories.label: Rejected asylum seekers:
categories.text: migrants who have applied for asylum and received a negative decision.

categories.label: Migrants in an irregular situation:
categories.text: people without a valid residence permit.

items.title: SESO service settles in
items.text: The service moves to Rue de Parme in Saint-Gilles and broadens its field of work by opening up to the neighbourhood and supporting asylum seekers and refugees from around the world.

items.title: First-line reception for asylum seekers
items.text: The social service commits to first-line reception work for asylum seekers within a specific small-scale reception structure.

items.title: Day nursery and mother-baby reception space
items.text: In partnership with the Early Childhood department of the Municipality of Saint-Gilles, the social service opens a day nursery and a mother-baby reception space for children of asylum seekers and people living in the Saint-Gilles neighbourhood.
